title: Internationalization and Locale Routing
summary: Organize routes and content for multiple languages or regions.
nestedConcepts: Keep translations separate from UI logic

subtopics.title: Choose a consistent locale route
subtopics.explanation: Choose a consistent locale format, such as `/fr/` or `/en-gb/`, and use it for links and metadata. Normalize locale codes so equivalent forms do not create duplicate routes. The route should make language choice clear without making every internal link hand-build a prefix.

subtopics.title: Keep translations separate from UI logic
subtopics.explanation: Store translated messages in locale dictionaries and use stable message keys in components. This lets translators update wording without changing application behavior. Avoid building sentences by concatenating fragments, because word order and grammar can differ across languages.

subtopics.title: Format values for each locale
subtopics.explanation: Use `Intl` formatters for dates, numbers, and currencies instead of hard-coding punctuation or symbols. A price such as 1,234.50 can use different separators and currency placement in another locale. Pass the intended locale and time zone so output is predictable.

subtopics.title: Support text direction and expansion
subtopics.explanation: Some languages read right to left, and translated phrases can be longer than the original. Use direction-aware layout rules and let text wrap instead of fixing widths around one language. Test a right-to-left locale and long translations before shipping.

subtopics.title: Plan locale-specific routing behavior
subtopics.explanation: Locale routes can affect canonical URLs, language alternates, redirects, and content availability. Decide how the default locale is represented and what happens when a translation is missing. Keep those rules consistent so users and search engines do not land on duplicate or empty pages.

foundations.overview: Internationalization prepares an app for different languages and regional formats. A locale-aware route can identify the language, while translation messages provide text. Dates, currencies, plural forms, and right-to-left layout also need attention.
foundations.mentalModel: A hotel directory uses room labels in the language each guest understands.
foundations.whyItMatters: Locale routing makes translated pages discoverable and keeps language choice consistent.

keyTakeaways: Choose a stable locale format for routes.
Keep translated messages outside component logic.
Format dates and numbers with Intl.
Support language-specific text direction and longer strings.
Avoid assuming every locale has the same URL needs.
